description: Are you ready to step into the shoes of a real vet? Join us for You Can Be a Veterinarian Camp, an immersive half-day experience where kids will explore the exciting world of veterinary medicine firsthand! From handling exotic animals to practicing real-life techniques, campers will gain valuable skills, interact with professional equipment, and even speak with veterinary experts. This rare opportunity offers a fun, hands-on journey into the world of animal care, inspiring future vets to learn, dream big, and discover their passion
what_is_included:
* **Exotics Physiology Lab:** You will get to show off your dexterity as you perform a dissection on a paper frog. You will also get an up-close encounter with one of our frogs and discover why amphibians are so unique.

* **Equine Care & Management 101:** Learn about the different aspects of equine care and the roles of the veterinarians, technicians and assistants while visiting the Equine Hospital.
 
* **Veterinary Surgical Nursing 100:** Meet and pet a snake while learning about a life-saving surgery that one of our Veterinarians performed on one of our scaly friends. Campers will practice surgical suturing of incisions on a life-like model.

* **Basics of Canine CPR & Intro to Anatomy:** Practice fundamental CPR techniques on a canine training model and view a respiratory demonstration. You will also get to learn what goes into prepping a dog for surgery.

* **Lagomorph Parasitology 100:** Interact with a rabbit and learn about the parasitic organisms that can affect these small mammals and others. You will view slides of bacteria under a microscope and discuss different treatment options.

itinerary:
* Campers rotate locations and activities every 30-45 min. They meet 3 different animals during certain activities and those are dispersed throughout the day. Campers also have a snack time which includes some free play.
* 15 minutes before program start: check in period, campers decorate their portfolios which are provided to them.
* 30 min: first activity. The class will discuss the day, camp rules, and icebreakers as well.
* 40 min: second activity
* 30 min: third activity.
* 30 min: snack period.
* 40 min: fourth activity.
* 30 min: fifth activity.
* 15 min at program end: check out period, campers stay circled up with their class and play quiet games.
highlights:

highlight_title: Veterinarian Camp is one of a kind!
highlight_description: Veterinarian Camp offers a rare opportunity for kids in San Diego to practice veterinary skills, interact with animals, and gain experience with equipment they might use in the future!
check_in_details: You can wait by our lobby and when check-in begins a side gate will be opened. Staff with clipboards will be there to check you in 10 minutes prior to start time. Once checked in, parents are free to leave and campers will be directed to their class table to place down their items, get their nametag, and get their portfolio. They can decorate their portfolio before camp starts. Once check-in has finished the class Instructor will assemble all the campers to go over expectations, the schedule of the day, and begin!
what_to_bring:
* **Snack**: Please pack snacks labeled with camper’s name. Snacks will be kept in the classroom. We do not have a refrigerator for campers and we do not have the ability to warm or cook snacks.
* **Water bottle**: Please pack a water bottle and be sure to label it with your child’s first and last name. We have a filtered water dispenser for refills throughout the day.
* **Comfortable clothes**: Have your child dress in comfortable clothes that are ok to get dirty. Dress in layers as needed by weather.
* **Sunscreen**: Children are half indoors and half outdoors with shaded areas. If you choose, you may leave sunscreen labeled with your name so your child can reapply sunscreen mid-day. Please let your child’s teacher know.
* **Cell phones/cameras**: Phones, cameras, and tablets may be brought. Your child can use them when instructed to help capture your child's experience, but only photos of the animals/activities can occur. Not all parents authorize pictures to be taken of their child. Please be mindful children are responsible for the items they bring.
special_requirements:
* If your child has an aide at school and you plan to have them attend with your child, or if you need to attend with your child, please call us at 858-756-4117 ext. 406 so that we can help them complete the fingerprint process. All aides MUST complete fingerprinting in order to attend and this process includes a livescan fee (paid to the livescan facility) and can take days or weeks to get results back.
* **Medication**: We must have a signed medical authorization release in order to give any medications to campers, which you can fill out during check-in and drop off any medication with the staff if it's needed by your child. Medications will be safely stored in the office. Please remember to pick them up at check-out.
* **Late fee policy**: Camp ends at 3:00pm. If your child(ren) are not picked up by 3:20pm you will be charged a late fee of $15 per camper, every 15 minutes.
 * **Transfer policy**: With 24 hours or more weekday notice we can transfer registrations which haven't started to another day, if that day has room, for the same camp, for any purpose.
* **Sick policy**: Communicate with us about child illness and we can discuss cancellation policy allowances. Please keep sick children home. Camp adheres to CDC guidelines.
* **Discipline policy**: Our camp staff are well trained and expected to resolve behavior issues in a positive manner. Our goal is to provide every child with a rewarding camp experience. At the beginning of the camp day, the camp teacher goes over camp rules. In the event that a rule is broken, the teacher gives the class a reminder. If the same child breaks a rule again, a verbal reminder directed at that child is issued including stating the problem and a solution. If a rule is broken again, the teacher will send the child to the office to think about the problem and discuss the problem/solution with the camp leadership. The camp leadership will call home to discuss behavior and a solution plan. Examples of behavior that will result in a camper being immediately asked to leave camp include, but are not limited to: destruction of property or disruptive behavior which threatens the safety of other campers, animals, volunteers, or staff. In such a case, camp fees are non-transferable and non-refundable.
restrictions:
* This camp is for kids only! Must be 9 or older for safety and maturity reasons with the activities and level of knowledge we provide.
* All campers must be able to use the restroom confidently and on their own.
* **Shoes**: For safety reasons, closed-toed shoes only. No sandals allowed.
* **Drawstrings**: For safety reasons, drawstrings (hoodies, pants or shorts) should not be worn on the playground.
* **Pets**: No pets are allowed on the campgrounds. There are no exceptions to this safety policy. Cannot leave pets alone in vehicles.
* **Toys, books, stuffed animals, etc.**: These may get soiled, broken, or lost—best to leave at home.
* **Sharp objects**: For safety purposes please leave anything that is a sharp or hazardous at home.

faqs:
**Why is this priced higher than your Critter Camps?**
In order to give campers the best and most hands-on experience with veterinary professionals and tools, we have to cover the costs of those increased services and materials. However this is an experience like no other and is truly demonstrating equipment and skills used in the industry!

**The camp is offered several times a year, is each one different?**
We run the same style of program on each date so they aren't designed to be different, but the half-day does have several different activities from the full-day!

**Will my child be watching surgeries and/or helping the veterinarians out?**
As amazing as that sounds, unfortunately neither situation will occur. We aren't equipped to run surgeries with an audience and we're not sure you'd get the most out of it without some fundamentals built up first. For safety purposes, we cannot have untrained people assisting with animal medical care, so while they will meet a veterinarian and see a hospital, they will be taking a tour and not actively assisting the staff.

**My child wants to work with animals, should they become a veterinarian?**
Veterinarian is often the first career we think of when it comes to working with animals, and it can be the perfect career for some people. However, pursuing the career is difficult, can be expensive, and might not be what everyone is looking for. There are a lot of ways you can work directly with animals, or indirectly support them. We discuss this at our career camps so join us to find out more!

**Authorized Pick Up & ID Checking**
For safety purposes we do not release children at pick up time to anyone not listed on the “authorized to pick up” list. We check ID daily at checkout time. To add someone to the authorized list, we must confirm you are one of the parents/guardians and then we can add any additional names, or you can log into your account and add more in yourself.
